core_obligations: Linearise the five hypotheses: (4) implies (3), (3) implies (1), and (1) implies (2), so that it suffices to treat case (2) (proof lines 3209-3218).

Replace Y by Spec(O_{Y,y}) using that this is the set of points specializing to y and that quasi-finiteness is stable under base change, so that Y = Spec(B) with B Noetherian local of dimension at most one and y the closed point (proof lines 3221-3228).

Reduce to X integral: if every fibre X_{i,y} of an irreducible component is discrete then so is X_y, and discreteness of the fibre is equivalent to quasi-finiteness at its points (proof lines 3231-3237).

Conclude by case distinction on the image of the generic point: if it maps to y then X is the spectrum of a finite extension of kappa(y); otherwise X factors through Spec(B/q) for a minimal prime q distinct from the maximal ideal, and the dimension formula together with dim(B/q) = 1 and the algebraicity of R(X) over kappa(q) yields the inequality 1 <= 1 - trdeg_{kappa(y)} kappa(x), hence trdeg = 0 and every point of X_y is closed in X_y (proof lines 3240-3265).
proof_roadmap: Reduce the alternatives to condition (2) (proof lines 3209-3218).
Pass to the local ring at y and to one irreducible component of X (proof lines 3221-3237).
Split off the case where the generic point maps to y (proof lines 3240-3242).
Apply the dimension formula in the remaining case to force the fibre to be discrete (proof lines 3243-3265).
difficulty_reason: For f: X to Y locally of finite type and a point y whose local ring is Noetherian of dimension at most one, the lemma gives five alternative hypotheses at generic points of X under which f is quasi-finite at every point of X lying over y (statement lines 3187-3206). The proof first linearises the hypotheses: (4) implies (3) because the quasi-finite locus is open and a dense open of a locally Noetherian scheme contains all generic points of irreducible components, (3) implies (1) by the equivalence between quasi-finiteness at a point and finiteness of the residue field extension there, and (1) implies (2) trivially (proof lines 3209-3218). The non-formal part is the main case: after replacing Y by Spec(O_{Y,y}) and X by one of its irreducible components (proof lines 3221-3237), the author distinguishes whether the generic point of X maps to y or to the other point of Spec(B), and in the second case applies the dimension formula to force the transcendence degree trdeg_{kappa(y)} kappa(x) to vanish, which makes every point of the fibre closed in the fibre (proof lines 3240-3265). The claim is H2: the reduction steps are standard, while the dimension formula computation is the substantive part.
